title: Cooking With What You Have
author: Priya Nair
body:
The best meals I've made were never the ones that followed a recipe exactly. They were the ones built from whatever was left in the fridge on a Tuesday night.

Recipes are useful as a starting education, but they teach you to follow instructions, not to cook. Improvisation teaches you why things work: why acid balances fat, why salt draws out flavor, why texture matters as much as taste.

![A cluttered kitchen counter with mismatched vegetables](images/cooking-with-what-you-have/counter.svg)

Next time you're missing an ingredient, don't go to the store. Figure out what's already in your kitchen that could do the same job.
